relevance_note: Single case report of a GFAP variant carrier with Alexander disease: "we report a case of type II Alexander disease (a subset of which was previously named “adult onset” or AOAD) in a man with a rare mutation in the GFAP gene"; the Discussion also gives individual-level facts on one previously published D128N carrier (ref [6]).
method_note: Letter-format case report, no tables; all rows hand-entered by the extractor and assembled with a short Python script that checks every span verbatim. Two in-scope people: 'patient' (the single case of this paper) and 'ref [6] patient' (a previously published 64-year-old male with D128N, given sex, age, variant and features in the Discussion). The paper says the two other D128N cases in refs [6, 7] 'most likely represent the same patient'; only one row was made, from the ref [6] description, and the ref [7] citation was not used as a separate person. The MR changes sentence ('MR changes included marked signal changes/atrophy of the bulbar region and cervical spinal cord.') follows the ref [6] patient's description and was attributed to that person; this attribution is a reading of sentence order. Variant string is printed 'c.382 G>A 9p.Asp128Asn' (the '9p.' appears to be a typesetting artefact for '(p.'); recorded verbatim, with protein part 'p.Asp128Asn' as a substring. Contradiction in the paper: the text says 'nucleotide position 383 of codon 128' but prints c.382 G>A. dbSNP rs267607509 is printed but is not a genomic coordinate, so genomic_coordinates is null. PolyPhen-2 'probably damaging' is an in-silico prediction, not an author classification or a functional assay, so pathogenicity and functional evidence are 'not reported'. Age at last evaluation for 'patient' is the age at the described hospitalization (52); he was followed for some years after and died 'a few years after his last medical follow-up', age at death not stated. Checklist: cerebral white matter and basal ganglia items are marked observed from neuropathology (demyelination; Rosenthal fibers in the periventricular zone of basal ganglia), although brain MRI showed 'no focal intracranial abnormality' (different modality, not treated as a contradiction). Periventricular rim excluded from 'No signal abnormalities were detected in the periventricular white matter in our patient'. Contrast enhancement excluded from the gadolinium spine MRI ('no enhancing lesions'). Spasticity/pyramidal signs left 'not reported' for 'patient': the paper attributes paraplegia to 'bulbar and pyramidal pathology' but names no pyramidal sign; dysarthria left 'not reported' because 'paresis and dysarthria ... as seen in this case' is ambiguous. Normal findings recorded per D-27: cervical discs normal -> 'cervical disc abnormality' excluded; HTLV-1 serology negative -> 'positive HTLV-1 serology' excluded. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not say its patient was described before.
